stem: Entropy is a measure of the disorder of a system.

parts.label: (a)
(b)
parts.text:
Place **one tick** ($\checkmark$) in **each row** of the table to show the sign of the entropy changes, $\Delta S$.

|  | $\Delta S$ is negative | $\Delta S$ is positive |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| solid dissolving in water |  |  |
| water boiling to steam |  |  |

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The equation for a reaction that produces methanol is shown.

$$\text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{OH}(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g})$$

Use relevant bond energies from the *Data Booklet* to calculate the enthalpy change, $\Delta H$, for this gas phase reaction.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
At $298\text{ K}$, both products of this reaction are liquid.

$$\text{CO}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{OH}(\text{l}) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) \quad \Delta H^\ominus = -131\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Standard entropies are shown in the table.

| substance | $\text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ | $\text{H}_2(\text{g})$ | $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}(\text{l})$ | $\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $S^\ominus/\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ | +214 | +131 | +127 | +70 |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the standard entropy change, $\Delta S^\ominus$, for this reaction.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the standard Gibbs free energy change, $\Delta G^\ominus$, for this reaction at $298\text{ K}$.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Predict the effect of increasing the temperature on the feasibility of this reaction.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem:
In a methanol-oxygen fuel cell, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}(\text{l})$ and $\text{O}_2(\text{g})$ are in contact with two inert electrodes immersed in an acidic solution.

The half-equation for the reaction at the methanol electrode is shown.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{OH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{CO}_2 + 6\text{H}^+ + 6\text{e}^- \quad E^\ominus = -0.02\text{ V}$$

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Use the *Data Booklet* to write an equation for the overall cell reaction.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Use $E^\ominus$ values to calculate the $E^\ominus_{\text{cell}}$ for this reaction.
